changes.title: Map marker briefs expanded
changes.detail: Conflict, military, energy, and economic markers now explain why they matter, status, and what to watch.

conflicts.name: Ukraine–Russia War
conflicts.recent: Continued deep strikes and front-line pressure; airspace and energy infrastructure remain contested.
conflicts.facts: Full-scale conflict ongoing since 2022 with high strategic and humanitarian cost.
conflicts.analysis: Neither side has achieved decisive breakthrough; attrition and long-range strike capacity dominate.

conflicts.name: Iran / Hormuz Theater
conflicts.recent: Reports of strikes, tanker incidents, and contested civilian-casualty claims around Hormuz approaches.
conflicts.facts: Strait of Hormuz remains a critical global oil chokepoint; residual proxy and direct exchange risk.
conflicts.analysis: Energy markets are the clearest real-time barometer of perceived escalation probability.

conflicts.name: Taiwan Strait Pressure
conflicts.recent: Elevated PLA air and naval activity including median-line crossings reported on an ongoing basis.
conflicts.facts: Critical semiconductor and Indo-Pacific deterrence node; activity remains below kinetic threshold.
conflicts.analysis: Pattern consistent with sustained pressure and threshold-testing rather than imminent invasion signals.

conflicts.name: Israel–Iran Axis Front
conflicts.actors: Israel, Iran, Lebanese and regional proxies
conflicts.recent: Multi-front posture continues with intermittent exchanges and proxy activity.
conflicts.facts: Direct and indirect exchanges have occurred in the broader regional cascade since 2023–26.
conflicts.analysis: Risk of wider regionalization remains elevated when energy and nuclear dossiers interact.

conflicts.name: Sudan Civil War
conflicts.actors: Sudanese Armed Forces, Rapid Support Forces
conflicts.recent: Fighting continues around strategic positions with severe civilian impact.
conflicts.facts: One of the world’s most severe ongoing humanitarian crises.
conflicts.analysis: Limited external mediation leverage; humanitarian access remains constrained.

conflicts.name: Yemen / Red Sea
conflicts.recent: Residual threat to Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb shipping lanes persists.
conflicts.facts: Secondary energy/shipping chokepoint; insurance and rerouting costs remain sensitive.
conflicts.analysis: Risk premium can reprice quickly on renewed interdiction claims.

markers.title: Ukraine–Russia War
markers.detail: Europe’s largest high-intensity war since 1945. Active front lines, long-range strikes, and contested airspace.
markers.why: Sets European security posture, NATO aid levels, and energy/grain risk pricing.
markers.watch: Deep strikes, front advances/retreats, NATO air-defense stocks, civilian infrastructure hits.

markers.title: Iran / Hormuz Theater
markers.detail: Direct and proxy exchanges involving Iran, US, Israel, and Gulf states near a global oil artery.
markers.why: Hormuz handles a large share of seaborne oil; kinetic risk here moves energy markets fast.
markers.watch: Tanker incidents, claimed strikes, Strait transit disruptions, Gulf air-defense alerts.

markers.title: Taiwan Strait Pressure
markers.detail: Sustained PLA air and naval activity around Taiwan; median-line crossings and exercises are common signals.
markers.why: Critical Indo-Pacific deterrence node and semiconductor supply-chain risk.
markers.watch: Sortie counts, naval block-training, US/partner transit operations, political crisis triggers.

markers.title: Israel–Iran Axis Front
markers.detail: Multi-front residual risk across Israel, Lebanon, Iran, and regional proxies after years of cascading exchanges.
markers.why: Can re-open wider Middle East escalation that interacts with energy and nuclear dossiers.
markers.watch: Northern front fire, deep-strike claims, proxy mobilization, ceasefire durability.

markers.title: Sudan Civil War
markers.detail: Fighting between Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces with severe civilian impact.
markers.why: One of the world’s worst active humanitarian crises; regional spillover into the Horn/Sahel.
markers.watch: Control of cities, famine indicators, external backers, humanitarian access.

markers.title: Yemen / Red Sea
markers.detail: Houthi and related activity creates residual interdiction risk on Red Sea shipping lanes.
markers.why: Affects Bab el-Mandeb traffic, insurance rates, and Asia–Europe container routing.
markers.watch: Ship attacks, coalition responses, insurance war-risk premiums, Suez diversion rates.

markers.title: Myanmar Civil War
markers.detail: Multi-front fighting between the military junta and resistance forces across the country.
markers.why: Regional refugee flows, border instability, and limited ASEAN mediation leverage.
markers.watch: Territory shifts, border clashes with neighbors, aid access, elite defections.

markers.title: Strait of Hormuz
markers.detail: Primary oil chokepoint linking Persian Gulf producers to global markets.
markers.why: Even temporary disruption can spike crude prices and inflation expectations worldwide.
markers.watch: Transit volume claims, naval escorts, mine/drone reports, oil futures reaction.

markers.title: Bab el-Mandeb / Red Sea
markers.detail: Secondary energy and container chokepoint between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
markers.why: Rerouting around Africa raises time/cost for Europe–Asia trade when risk rises.
markers.watch: Attack reports, carrier diversions, war-risk insurance, Suez Canal throughput.

markers.title: Persian Gulf Energy Complex
markers.detail: Cluster of major producers and export terminals (Saudi, UAE, Kuwait, Iraq, Iran exports).
markers.why: Production and export security here anchors global spare capacity narratives.
markers.watch: Facility security incidents, OPEC+ signals, export terminal disruptions.

markers.title: US Markets / New York
markers.detail: Major equity, rates, and risk-sentiment node. Public market moves often lag geopolitical shocks by hours to days.
markers.why: Shows how investors price conflict, energy, and policy risk in real time.
markers.watch: VIX/equity swings after kinetic headlines, energy equities, USD safe-haven moves.

markers.title: London / Europe Energy & Defense
markers.detail: European exposure to Middle East energy flows, Russian residual risk, and elevated defense spending.
markers.why: European gas, power prices, and defense budgets react strongly to Ukraine and Hormuz risk.
markers.watch: TTF gas prices, defense stock moves, UK/EU policy statements after escalation.

markers.title: Tokyo / Indo-Pacific Trade
markers.detail: Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing supply-chain node sensitive to Taiwan Strait risk.
markers.why: Japan is a core US ally and a critical chip/equipment supplier; Strait shocks hit Asian markets first.
markers.watch: Yen risk-off moves, chip equities, Japanese defense posture statements.
